text.en: In the exclusive first-person plural, the pronominal form is *cóka*, or optionally *cóka 'utar* when emphasizing a large group, with plural grammatical number denoting two or more individuals on the speaker's side to the exclusion of the addressee ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-exclusive-first-person-plural-has-the-pronoun⟧. This person may refer to two or more individuals speaking at the same time or, far more commonly, it includes third parties associated with the speaker whether they are present or not ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-exclusive-first-person-plural-may-denote-two⟧. In colloquial speech, the transitive subject marker is the prefix *ci-*, which has the allomorph *c-* before vowels other than *i*, and appears before consonants or on copulas and nouns in the belonging form ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--ci-as-restricted-to-cohesive-known-group⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-first-person-plural-nominative-is-expressed-by⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-first-person-plural-nominative-is-expressed-by-2⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-exclusive-first-person-plural-transitive-subjective-personal⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-exclusive-first-person-plural-transitive-prefix-ci⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-transitive-verbs-the-exclusive-first-person-plural⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-first-person-plural-exclusive-subject-is-marked⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-exclusive-first-person-plural-has-the-pronoun⟧. The intransitive subject marker is the suffix *-as* (or *-ash* / *-'ás*) ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--ci-as-restricted-to-cohesive-known-group⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-first-person-plural-nominative-is-expressed-by⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-first-person-plural-nominative-is-expressed-by-3⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--first-person-plural-subject-marker-as-is-used⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-exclusive-first-person-plural-intransitive-subjective-personal⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-intransitive-verbs-the-exclusive-first-person-plural⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-first-person-plural-exclusive-subject-is-marked⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-exclusive-first-person-plural-has-the-pronoun⟧. In the Ishikari dialect, the intransitive suffixes *-an* and *-as* combine with second-person object markers to function as transitive subject suffixes, producing combinations such as *e-...-an* and *es-...-as* ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-the-ishikari-dialect-the-intransitive-first-person⟧. When quoting the speech of multiple third persons in the Saru dialect, quotative forms are almost always used, though ordinary exclusive forms rarely occur ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--when-quoting-the-speech-of-multiple-third-persons⟧. The objective marker across dialects, including Saru and Shizunai, is the prefix *un-* (or *'un-*), meaning 'us (excluding addressee)' ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--shizunai-first-plural-objective-un⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-the-saru-dialect-first-person-plural-object⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-exclusive-first-person-plural-objective-personal-affix⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-first-person-plural-exclusive-objective-person-affix⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-exclusive-first-person-plural-has-the-pronoun⟧. In Shizunai, *ci-*, *-as*, and *un-* belong to colloquial speech and are restricted to referring to a cohesive, clearly defined, known group that the speaker represents and speaks for ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--ci-as-restricted-to-cohesive-known-group⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--un-subject-to-same-restrictions-as-ci⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-prefix-ci-is-used-for-first-person⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-the-shizunai-dialect-ci-is-used-for⟧. Kindaichi lists the same functions for *ci-* as for *a-*, excluding the passive voice and the honorific second person ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--kindaichi-lists-the-same-functions-for-ci-as⟧. In *kamuy yukar* epics, the narrator or protagonist uses these exclusive markers—*coka*, *ci=*, *=as*, and *un=*—for self-reference as a kind of pluralis majestatis or elevated first person, with *ci-* marking elevated nominative singular or plural and *un-* marking elevated objective ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-kamuy-yukar-folktales-the-protagonist-uses-first⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-transitive-prefix-c-i-is-the-first⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-the-language-of-kamuy-yukar-mythic-epics⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-the-language-of-kamuy-yukar-un-is⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-god-songs-kamuy-yukar-the-first-person⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-divine-songs-kamuy-yukar-exclusively-some-dialects⟧. In the Saru and Chitose dialects, this divine speech register is also found outside verse in the sound imitation of an owl's call, *pewrep ci=koyki!* ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-the-saru-and-chitose-dialects-the-sound⟧.
text.ja: 除外的一人称複数において、代名詞形は *cóka* であり、大勢を強調する際には任意で *cóka 'utar* が用いられ、聞き手を含まない話し手側の2人以上を指す文法上の複数である ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-exclusive-first-person-plural-has-the-pronoun⟧。これは2人以上が同時に発話する場合を指すこともあれば、その場にいるか否かを問わず話し手側に属する第三者を含む場合もあり、後者のほうがはるかに一般的である ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-exclusive-first-person-plural-may-denote-two⟧。口語において、他動詞主格標識は接頭辞 *ci-* であり、*i* 以外の母音の前では異形態 *c-* をとり、子音の前やコピュラおよび名詞の所属形に付加される ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--ci-as-restricted-to-cohesive-known-group⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-first-person-plural-nominative-is-expressed-by⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-first-person-plural-nominative-is-expressed-by-2⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-exclusive-first-person-plural-transitive-subjective-personal⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-exclusive-first-person-plural-transitive-prefix-ci⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-transitive-verbs-the-exclusive-first-person-plural⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-first-person-plural-exclusive-subject-is-marked⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-exclusive-first-person-plural-has-the-pronoun⟧。自動詞主格標識は接尾辞 *-as*（または *-ash*、*-'ás*）である ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--ci-as-restricted-to-cohesive-known-group⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-first-person-plural-nominative-is-expressed-by⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-first-person-plural-nominative-is-expressed-by-3⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--first-person-plural-subject-marker-as-is-used⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-exclusive-first-person-plural-intransitive-subjective-personal⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-intransitive-verbs-the-exclusive-first-person-plural⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-first-person-plural-exclusive-subject-is-marked⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-exclusive-first-person-plural-has-the-pronoun⟧。石狩方言では、自動詞接尾辞 *-an* および *-as* が二人称目的語接辞と結合して他動詞主語接尾辞として用いられ、*e-...-an* や *es-...-as* などの組み合わせを作る ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-the-ishikari-dialect-the-intransitive-first-person⟧。沙流方言において複数の第三者の発話の引用ではほとんどの場合引用形が用いられるが、まれに通常の除外的形が現れることもある ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--when-quoting-the-speech-of-multiple-third-persons⟧。沙流や静内を含む諸方言における目的格標識は、聞き手を含まない「私達を」を意味する接頭辞 *un-*（または *'un-*）である ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--shizunai-first-plural-objective-un⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-the-saru-dialect-first-person-plural-object⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-exclusive-first-person-plural-objective-personal-affix⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-first-person-plural-exclusive-objective-person-affix⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-exclusive-first-person-plural-has-the-pronoun⟧。静内方言において *ci-*、*-as*、*un-* は口語に属し、話し手が代表して発言できる明確に定義された既知のまとまりある集団を指すことに制約される ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--ci-as-restricted-to-cohesive-known-group⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--un-subject-to-same-restrictions-as-ci⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-prefix-ci-is-used-for-first-person⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-the-shizunai-dialect-ci-is-used-for⟧。金田一は受動態と敬称二人称を除いて *ci-* に *a-* と同様の機能を挙げている ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--kindaichi-lists-the-same-functions-for-ci-as⟧。神謡（カムイユカル）において主人公や叙述者は、威厳の複数あるいは雅語第I人称として自身を指すために *coka*、*ci=*、*=as*、*un=* などの除外標識を用い、*ci-* は単複の主格に、*un-* は目的格に用いられる ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-kamuy-yukar-folktales-the-protagonist-uses-first⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-transitive-prefix-c-i-is-the-first⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-the-language-of-kamuy-yukar-mythic-epics⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-the-language-of-kamuy-yukar-un-is⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-god-songs-kamuy-yukar-the-first-person⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-divine-songs-kamuy-yukar-exclusively-some-dialects⟧。沙流方言および千歳方言では、神謡外であってもフクロウの鳴き声の聞きなしである *pewrep ci=koyki!* にカムイの言葉として一人称複数の接辞 *ci=* が用いられている ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-the-saru-and-chitose-dialects-the-sound⟧。

text.en: In affirmative clauses, verbal agreement for the first-person plural exclusive exhibits a tripartite alignment that distinguishes the transitive subject *ci=*, the intransitive subject *=as*, and the object *un=* ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--first-plural-exclusive-tripartite-alignment⟧. This contrasts with the inclusive set in affirmative clauses, which also shows tripartite alignment distinguishing the transitive subject *a=*, the intransitive subject *=an*, and the object *i=* ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--first-plural-inclusive-tripartite-alignment⟧. In the Saru dialect, the exclusive subject of a single-argument verb takes the suffix *-as*, whereas the subject of a two-argument or three-argument verb takes the prefix *ci-* ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-the-saru-dialect-the-first-person-plural⟧. In the Shizunai dialect, whenever an intransitive verb combines with a nominative pronominal affix that alternates between a prefix and a suffix—namely the first-person plural and the indefinite person—it obligatorily takes the suffixal form ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--when-combined-with-a-nominative-pronominal-affix-that⟧. In Sakhalin Ainu, the first-person plural affix *'an* prefixes to transitive verbs as *'an=* and suffixes to intransitive verbs as *='an* ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--sakhalin-an-affix-transitive-prefix-intransitive-suffix⟧.
text.ja: 肯定節において、一人称複数除外の動詞一致は3分割型アラインメントを示し、他動詞主語 *ci=*、自動詞主語 *=as*、目的語 *un=* がそれぞれ区別される ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--first-plural-exclusive-tripartite-alignment⟧。これは他動詞主語 *a=*、自動詞主語 *=an*、目的語 *i=* を区別する肯定節の一人称複数包括の3分割型アラインメントと対照をなす ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--first-plural-inclusive-tripartite-alignment⟧。沙流方言では、1項動詞の一人称複数除外主語は接尾辞 *-as* で標示されるのに対し、2項または3項動詞の主語は接頭辞 *ci-* で標示される ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-the-saru-dialect-the-first-person-plural⟧。静内方言において、接頭辞形と接尾辞形の交替をもつ主格人称接辞（一人称複数および不定人称）と結合する際、自動詞は常に接尾辞形をとる ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--when-combined-with-a-nominative-pronominal-affix-that⟧。樺太アイヌ語では、一人称複数接辞 *'an* は他動詞には *'an=* として前接し、自動詞には *='an* として後接する ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--sakhalin-an-affix-transitive-prefix-intransitive-suffix⟧。

text.en: In colloquial conversation, the first-person plural form is strictly exclusive, referring to 'we' without the hearer, while an inclusive 'we' that includes the addressee is marked by the fourth person ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-daily-conversation-the-first-person-plural-form⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--when-we-excludes-the-addressee-the-first-person⟧. The exclusive forms use the transitive subject *ci-*, the intransitive subject *-as* (or *-ash* in Class II division i verbs such as *itak(-pa)-ash*), and the object *un-*, whereas the inclusive forms use the transitive subject *a-*, the intransitive subject *-an* (as in *itak(-pa)-an*), and the object *i-* ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-intransitive-verbs-the-exclusive-first-person-plural⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-transitive-verbs-the-exclusive-first-person-plural⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-the-spoken-language-the-first-person-plural⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-the-colloquial-register-class-ii-division-i⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-inclusive-first-person-plural-transitive-subjective-personal⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-inclusive-first-person-plural-intransitive-subjective-personal⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-inclusive-first-person-plural-objective-personal-affix⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-first-person-plural-inclusive-objective-person-affix⟧. The inclusive category possesses the independent pronoun *'a'oká* (or *'a'oká 'utar* for a large group) with the indexes *'a-*, *-án*, and *'i-*, which strictly speaking designates a '1st-2nd person' encompassing speaker and addressee, contrasting with *cóka* as the plural counterpart to singular *káni* ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-inclusive-first-person-plural-has-the-pronoun⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-pronoun-that-strictly-corresponds-as-the-plural⟧. Colloquial clusivity categories developed by employing the first-person affixes of Classical Ainu as inclusive markers, where *a-* is treated as fundamentally an inclusive prefix by Kindaichi and Chiri ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--kindaichi-and-chiri-view-a-basically-as-a⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-exclusive-inclusive-categories-in-colloquial-ainu-developed⟧. In poetic style, *un-* acts as a first-person objective, and *i-* in *i-sikerayke* serves as an elevated first-person plural objective marker ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-prefix-un-is-used-as-the-first⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-prefix-i-in-i-sikerayke-functions-as⟧. In daily speech, the suffix *-an* is restricted to plural verbs such as *arki-an* 'we come' and is never used with singular *ek*, but in the elegant language of Saru and Chitose, *-an* can occur with singular verbs such as *ek-an* 'I am coming' ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-everyday-language-the-first-person-plural-personal⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-the-elegant-language-of-the-saru-and⟧. In the Shizunai dialect, inclusive reference is not an independent grammatical category of the first person plural but is analyzed as a function of the indefinite person *a-* / *an-*, which is used whenever the group is not a small, cohesive, speaker-represented unit, while *ci-* is never used for the indefinite person ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--shizunai-lacks-clusivity-distinction⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--ci-never-used-for-indefinite⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-indefinite-person-is-employed-for-the-1st⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--when-the-conditions-of-a-small-cohesive-and⟧. In the dialogue of the *Ainu Shin'yōshū* (Horobetsu dialect), characters' speech contains a mixture of first-person plural forms like *ci=rewsire* and fourth-person forms like *a=rewsire* for the same situation, even though narrative prose is uniformly in the first-person plural ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-the-ainu-shin-y-sh-horobetsu-dialect⟧. Unlike Hokkaido dialects, Sakhalin Ainu lacks the exclusive affixes *ci-* and *-as*, as well as the clusivity distinction, employing *an-* / *-an* for both inclusive and exclusive reference; moreover, in the northern west coast of Sakhalin, first-person plural affixes are sometimes used in place of singular forms ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--west-coast-sakhalin-ainu-lost-the-first-person⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-the-dialects-of-the-northern-part-of⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--unlike-hokkaido-dialects-karafuto-ainu-lacks-first-person⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--unlike-hokkaido-dialects-karafuto-ainu-lacks-a-clusivity⟧.
text.ja: 日常会話において一人称複数形は厳密に除外的であり、聞き手を含まない「私たち」に限って用いられ、聞き手を含む包括的な「私たち」は4人称形で表される ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-daily-conversation-the-first-person-plural-form⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--when-we-excludes-the-addressee-the-first-person⟧。除外的形式は他動詞主格 *ci-*、自動詞主格 *-as*（第II類第 i 種動詞では *itak(-pa)-ash* のように *-ash*）、目的格 *un-* を用いるのに対し、包括的形式は他動詞主格 *a-*、自動詞主格 *-an*（*itak(-pa)-an* など）、目的格 *i-* を用いる ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-intransitive-verbs-the-exclusive-first-person-plural⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-transitive-verbs-the-exclusive-first-person-plural⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-the-spoken-language-the-first-person-plural⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-the-colloquial-register-class-ii-division-i⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-inclusive-first-person-plural-transitive-subjective-personal⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-inclusive-first-person-plural-intransitive-subjective-personal⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-inclusive-first-person-plural-objective-personal-affix⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-first-person-plural-inclusive-objective-person-affix⟧。包括的範疇は代名詞 *'a'oká*（大勢には *'a'oká 'utar*）と接辞 *'a-*、*-'án*、*'i-* を持ち、厳密には話し手と聞き手を含む「1-2人称」と呼ぶべきものであって、単数 *káni* に対する複数代名詞である *cóka* と対比される ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-inclusive-first-person-plural-has-the-pronoun⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-pronoun-that-strictly-corresponds-as-the-plural⟧。口語の包括／除外の範疇は古典アイヌ語の一人称接辞を包括形として用いることで発達したものであり、金田一と知里は *a-* を基本的に一人称複数包括接辞とみなしている ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--kindaichi-and-chiri-view-a-basically-as-a⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-exclusive-inclusive-categories-in-colloquial-ainu-developed⟧。雅語において *un-* は一人称目的格として機能し、*i-sikerayke* における接頭辞 *i-* は雅語一人称複数目的格接辞として現れる ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-prefix-un-is-used-as-the-first⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-prefix-i-in-i-sikerayke-functions-as⟧。日常語では接辞 *-an* は常に複数動詞と結合して *arki-an* のように用いられ、単数動詞 *ek* とは用いられないが、沙流および千歳の雅定語では *ek-an*「私は来る」のように単数動詞とも結合する ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-everyday-language-the-first-person-plural-personal⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-the-elegant-language-of-the-saru-and⟧。静内方言には一人称複数の包括・除外の区別が存在せず、包括的指示は不定人称 *a-* / *an-* の機能として分析され、少人数で結束し話し手が代表する集団という条件が満たされない場合に用いられる一方、*ci-* が不定人称のために用いられることはない ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--shizunai-lacks-clusivity-distinction⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--ci-never-used-for-indefinite⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-indefinite-person-is-employed-for-the-1st⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--when-the-conditions-of-a-small-cohesive-and⟧。『アイヌ神謡集』（幌別方言）では地の文が一貫して一人称複数形で語られるのに対し、登場人物のせりふ中では同一状況に対して *ci=rewsire* のような一人称複数形と *a=rewsire* のような4人称形が混在する ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-the-ainu-shin-y-sh-horobetsu-dialect⟧。北海道方言と異なり、樺太アイヌ語には排他接辞 *ci-* および *-as* や包括対除外の区別が存在せず、*an-* / *-an* が両方に用いられるほか、樺太西海岸北部方言では一人称複数形が一人称単数形の代わりに用いられることもある ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--west-coast-sakhalin-ainu-lost-the-first-person⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-the-dialects-of-the-northern-part-of⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--unlike-hokkaido-dialects-karafuto-ainu-lacks-first-person⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--unlike-hokkaido-dialects-karafuto-ainu-lacks-a-clusivity⟧。

text.en: In Iburi excluding the Mukawa area, the colloquial incorporating conjugation marks a first-person nominative subject acting on a second-person object by means of the suffix *-ash*, as in *e-kore-ash*, *echi-kore-ash*, and *i-kore-ash* ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-iburi-excluding-the-mukawa-area-the-first⟧. In Sakhalin Ainu elder speech, the first-person plural affix *'an* is used as a first-person singular affix ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--sakhalin-elder-speech-an-singular⟧.
text.ja: 鵡川地方を除く胆振の口語における抱合的活用では、二人称目的語に対する一人称主格が接尾辞 *-ash* で表され、*e-kore-ash*、*echi-kore-ash*、*i-kore-ash* などの形をとる ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-iburi-excluding-the-mukawa-area-the-first⟧。樺太アイヌ語の老人ことばでは、一人称複数接辞 *'an* が一人称単数接辞として用いられる ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--sakhalin-elder-speech-an-singular⟧。

text.en: The exclusive first-person plural transitive subject prefix *ci-* drops its vowel before vowel-initial verb stems, surfacing as *c=* before /a, e, o, u/ in Southern Hokkaido and generally before vowels ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-southern-hokkaido-the-prefix-ci-first-person⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-vowel-i-of-the-first-person-prefix⟧. For Class II verbs, first-person subject markers appear as suffixes, as seen in *chish-an* 'I weep' ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--for-class-ii-verbs-first-person-subject-markers⟧. The indefinite derivational prefix *ci-* is homophonous with the exclusive first-person plural transitive subject prefix *ci-* ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-indefinite-derivational-prefix-ci-is-homophonous-with⟧. In addition, the prefix *chi-* has a universal person function that derives nominals such as *chi-mi-p* 'clothing', *chi-o-ipe-p* 'tableware', *chi-e-ninui-pe* 'pillow', and *chi-nunuke-i* 'genitals' ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-prefix-chi-has-a-universal-person-function⟧.
text.ja: 除外的一人称複数他動詞主格接頭辞 *ci-* は母音で始まる語幹の前で母音を脱落させ、北海道南部方言において /a, e, o, u/ の前で *c=* となり、一般に母音の前で *c-* となる ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--in-southern-hokkaido-the-prefix-ci-first-person⟧⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-vowel-i-of-the-first-person-prefix⟧。第II類動詞では一人称主語標識が接尾辞として現れ、*chish-an*「我泣く」のような例がある ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--for-class-ii-verbs-first-person-subject-markers⟧。不定人称派生接頭辞 *ci-* は除外的一人称複数他動詞主格の人称接頭辞と同形である ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-indefinite-derivational-prefix-ci-is-homophonous-with⟧。また接頭辞 *chi-* には汎称の用法が存在し、*chi-mi-p*「着物」、*chi-o-ipe-p*「食器」、*chi-e-ninui-pe*「枕」、*chi-nunuke-i*「陰部」などの名詞を派生する ⟦claim:person/first-person-plural-and-clusivity--the-prefix-chi-has-a-universal-person-function⟧。
